notes.title: Patch 1
notes.content:
Hello gamers, our first little update is live now!

[h2]Fixed:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Achievements not firing after credits roll
[*]The Salesman appears at the wrong staff door when immediately re-entering Meggs after "In for a Penny"
[*]Menu/UI Sound Effects not altered by the volume setting
[*]Screen resolution displayed as Height x Width
[*]Misc. animation and collision issues
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues:[/h2]
[list]
[*]In some rare cases the game's audio plugin has trouble detecting DAC devices, potentially due issues with the plugin detecting ASIO drivers. If you experience this issue, please try disabling/enabling your other devices or switching the DAC out of ASIO mode if possible. We've not been able to reproduce this in house, so If the problem persists please send us a message with the device details to help@thankgoodness.game
[*]The game was drawn and designed for a fixed 16:9 ratio, so ultrawide monitors or other resolutions outside this ratio will experience pillar/letterboxing
[/list]

Goodnight gamers x

notes.title: Thank Goodness You're Here! review: edges towards greatness and won't take you long to beat
notes.content:
British comedy is too often defined by its relationship to America: either as merely irony and sarcasm, which we're told Americans don't understand, or as a sprightly ideas factory for works such as The Office, which Americans can bless by re-making at scale.

Peel back the curtains of American cultural hegemony however and you may find the true pulsing core of British comedy that lies beneath: innuendo. No American network is in a bidding war to import Vic and Bob or remake Bottom, and Carry On and Benny Hill are assumed to be anachronisms in our modern times, but Thank Goodness You're Here! enters the conversation with a nudge and a wink. It's a cheeky 2-3 hour adventure through a small northern town, and it's here to educate the entire world of our nation's obsession with sausages and bare bottoms.
